title: What does XChainModifyBridge do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of XChainModifyBridge and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, XChainModifyBridge changes supported parameters of an existing bridge. [1]

The caller must have the authority required for that bridge, and only documented mutable settings can change. Review rewards and account-creation parameters together with existing transfer workflows. A configuration update is not a completed cross-chain payment. Parties still need to reconcile commitments and claims under the applicable bridge definition on both networks. [1]

The XChainModifyBridge reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using XChainModifyBridge, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
